stories.title: All election guarantees fulfilled, says Arvind Kejriwal; Opposition slams AAP of misusing public resources
stories.summary: The Opposition parties accuse AAP of misusing Punjab’s public resources to organise a party event while the State grapples with a mounting financial crisis
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ahead of the Assembly elections in Punjab, due in early 2027, Aam Aadmi Party’s national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) urged women to persuade the men in their families to vote for the AAP.

He was speaking at a rally in Moga on the party’s foundation day, where he highlighted the ₹1,000 financial assistance provided by the AAP Government to help women deal with inflation, taking a dig at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Government at the Centre.
The Opposition parties, meanwhile, targeted the AAP, accusing it of misusing Punjab’s public resources to organise a party event while the State grapples with a mounting financial crisis.

Mr. Kejriwal claimed that the AAP had fulfilled all its election guarantees within five years, adding that the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP had announced that they would discontinue the AAP Government’s existing schemes if voted to power.
“I am standing before people of Punjab today because my ‘Chota Bhai’, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, has fulfilled all of Kejriwal’s guarantees.
We promised free electricity and people are getting free electricity.
We promised to organise ‘tirth yatra,’ and now devotees are going on the ‘yatra.’ We promised to open Aam Aadmi Clinics and now people are receiving great treatment.
We promised free treatment, and everyone has been provided with a health insurance card worth ₹10 lakh,” he said.
The Smart Ration Card Scheme to extend food security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries was also launched at the event.

Leader of the Opposition in the Punjab Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa alleged that the Government machinery, including State-owned buses, administrative resources and police personnel were deployed for a political function at the expense of the public exchequer.
“Before calling it a ‘Khushhaal Rally’, the AAP must answer a fundamental question: has Punjab actually become prosperous under its rule?
When the State is drowning in debt, why is public money being spent on a party celebration?

stories.headline: Election Commission fixes website flaw exposing voter data after Reuters findings
stories.title: Election Commission fixes website flaw exposing voter data after Reuters findings
stories.summary: Researchers say flaw could have been easily ​abused
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A security flaw in India’s Election Commission (ECI) website that was allowing access to sensitive personal details and documents of some voters has been fixed, after Reuters discovered the vulnerability and alerted the institution.
Researchers said the flaw, which Reuters is the first to report, could have been easily abused.

The security issue, and the fix, come months ahead of elections in key Indian states, including the most populous, Uttar Pradesh, and while the ECI is facing growing public anger over a contentious drive to update voter lists.
Opposition parties and activists have said the drive has disenfranchised millions of voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI says it has complied with all regulations, while the BJP argues opposition groups are misleading the country after failing to win elections.

A Reuters review over more than a month of the ECI’s website showed that when a voter logged into their account and requested a telephone call with their local electoral officer, the network tab in an ordinary browser’s developer tools, opened with a simple right click, started showing the reference number of the form submitted online to enrol as voters or update their information.

On using those reference numbers to book the call, the same network details started revealing personal information such as the name, phone number, email, date of birth and address of the user, and even file paths to identification documents like passports that were submitted.

Such details were not otherwise visible on the browser’s main screen, which pointed to a vulnerability in the website’s code, said Indian security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed, who reviewed the Reuters findings step by step on the ECI website.
The bigger concern, researchers said, was the reference numbers followed a predictable pattern, meaning hackers could guess them, and automate downloads of large amounts of data.
A lay user is unlikely to follow such steps while requesting a call, but cybercriminals could, and also automate the steps to harvest data in bulk and abuse it, they said.
Reuters first shared its findings and sought comment from the ECI and its three commissioners on October 26, but they did not respond despite repeated requests.
On Thursday, an ECI spokesman said the commission’s information technology division had been asked to look into the findings.

article_sentences: - The Supreme Court confined Friday’s contempt hearing to compliance with its one-time order permitting the ceremonial lamp to be lit at Deepathoon on 24 November.
- The Archaeological Survey of India said police blocked its team from reaching the lamp.
Counsel for the Madurai Collector said ASI officials had been consulted at several meetings.
- Tamil Nadu apologised to the court on Wednesday and held temple authorities responsible for the lamp being lit only at its customary site.

The Supreme Court on Friday warned that it would act against anyone seeking to create “constitutional chaos” as it heard contempt petitions over the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the disputed Deepathoon pillar on Thirupparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu.
A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said its orders could not be diluted.
It said the hearing would focus on compliance with its 20 November order, which granted one-time permission to light the lamp at Deepathoon on 24 November.
The hearing was continuing.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), told the bench that local police stopped the agency’s team at about 3 pm on 24 November and prevented it from approaching the lamp.
He said the temple trustees had told the team they had received no instructions from senior officials about allowing it through.
Mehta described the authorities’ conduct as “aggravated contempt” and asked the court to have the lamp lit at Deepathoon before hearing those facing contempt proceedings.
He also sought oversight by another agency.

stories.title: Senior Advocate Faisal Qadri Appointed Jammu and Kashmir Advocate General
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 27 : The Jammu and Kashmir Government on Friday appointed Senior Advocate Faisal Qadri as the new Advocate General of the Union Territory. The Formal order appointing Qadri was issued on Friday after the Raj Bhavan cleared his name for the post. Three names; Advocate Faisal Qadri, Advocate Ishaq Qadri and Advocate Seema Shekhar had been sent to the Raj Bhavan for consideration for the top legal position. Qadri's appointment was formalised following the clearance from the Raj Bhavan.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

opening: Srinagar, Nov 27: The Jammu and Kashmir Government on Friday appointed Senior Advocate Faisal Qadri as the new Advocate General of the Union Territory.
The Formal order appointing Qadri was issued on Friday after the Raj Bhavan cleared his name for the post.
body: Three names; Advocate Faisal Qadri, Advocate Ishaq Qadri and Advocate Seema Shekhar had been sent to the Raj Bhavan for consideration for the top legal position.
Qadri's appointment was formalised following the clearance from the Raj Bhavan.
Srinagar, Nov 27: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha has approved the appointment of senior advocate Faisal Qadri as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir.
Qadri will serve as the government's chief legal adviser and represent the Union Territory in legal matters before the High Court and other courts.
The appointment fills the position of Advocate General, which had remained vacant since October 2024.
Qadri is a senior advocate practising before the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court.

The appointment was notified by the Department of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs through Government Order S.O. 329, issued by order of Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha under Section 79(1) of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
The notification, signed by Commissioner/Secretary to the Government Achal Sethi, lays down the terms of appointment, remuneration, allowances and professional fees payable to the Advocate General.
Under the order, Qadri will receive a monthly remuneration of ₹1 lakh and will be entitled to rent-free furnished accommodation at either Jammu or Srinagar.
If he opts to reside in his own house, he will receive a compensatory allowance of ₹12,000 per month.
He will also be provided an official vehicle free of charge for use within and outside city limits, besides a monthly sumptuary allowance of ₹3,000.
The order provides for medical reimbursement and travel allowances at the rates admissible to a sitting Judge of the High Court.
His headquarters will be the same as that of the High Court, unless otherwise directed by the government.
The Home Department will provide him security as required.
Fee structure for court appearances.
The notification also prescribes a detailed fee structure for the Advocate General's professional work.
For each contested writ petition, appeal, suit or civil appeal conducted on behalf of the Union Territory before the High Court, Qadri will receive a fee of ₹5,000.

For appearances before the Supreme Court, Delhi High Court and other courts and tribunals outside Jammu and Kashmir, the fee has been fixed at ₹50,000 for each effective hearing and ₹5,000 for each non-effective hearing.
He will also be paid ₹50,000 per conference in cases before the Supreme Court and Delhi High Court.
In arbitration matters within the Union Territory, the prescribed fee will be ₹10,000 per effective hearing and ₹3,000 per non-effective hearing.
For arbitration cases outside the UT, the rates will be ₹25,000 and ₹5,000, respectively.

The order clarifies that no separate fee will be payable for providing legal opinions to the government, attending meetings or consultations with government functionaries or bodies wholly owned or controlled by it, or appearing before the High Court in criminal and contempt cases.

stories.title: Cabinet clears women’s quota Bill with ‘50%’ change that may tilt the balance

article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared the Constitution Amendment Bill to implement reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures through a delimitation exercise that would increase Lok Sabha seats in all states by 50 per cent, sources said.
The current inter-state ratio of constituencies in both Houses, based on the 1971 population, will be sealed till 2051, sources said.
The fresh Bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased seats, the sources said.

The Bill, which was introduced during a special session in April but failed to clear the Lok Sabha with a two-thirds majority, did not have the provision for the 50 per cent increase in the number of seats in all states.
The government announced on Thursday that it has requested the presiding officers of both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha to reconvene to transact essential government business.
The Lok Sabha will meet for a four-day special session starting Monday, November 30, and the Rajya Sabha will meet on December 2.

Government sources have said that the special session, which is an extension of the Monsoon Session that was adjourned sine die on August 13 but was not prorogued, is for a fresh push to the delimitation package, which includes implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and the state legislatures as well as the expansion of the Lok Sabha.

The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, met at 1 pm on Friday and cleared a few amendments to ensure that no state loses its representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to other states after delimitation, sources said.

MK Stalin, leader of the DMK, one of the parties expected to extend support to the Bill in its latest form, reiterated on Friday that Tamil Nadu’s existing share of seats in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced.

“If the number of parliamentary constituencies is increased, under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18% share of seats in the lower house be reduced… The existing proportion of parliamentary representation among States, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain frozen for another 25 years,” Stalin posted on X.
Sources in the DMK said the party, which had opposed the Bill in its earlier form, is expected to extend its support if their conditions are met.
Besides the DMK, NCP’s Sharad Pawar-led faction and a few other smaller parties are expected to support the Bill, sources said.

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday approved a proposal to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha by 50% across states, with the revised ceiling to remain in place until 2051, sources told TOI.
The decision comes ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, during which the government is expected to take up changes to the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill.

The proposed increase in Lok Sabha seats is understood to be part of the government's efforts to address concerns over the impact of delimitation on the representation of states, particularly those in southern India.
Earlier reports had indicated that the government was considering a formula to increase seats by 50% across states while retaining their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.
The Cabinet meeting, chaired by PM Modi, was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to remain present, sources told ANI.
The government is considering amendments to the earlier legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
The proposed changes follow the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha in April.
The earlier Bill linked the implementation of women's reservation to delimitation and proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850.
The special sitting of Parliament will begin with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2.
The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.
Ayush Pandey is a journalist at The Times of India, covering breaking news, politics, defence, and major legal and policy developments across India and the world.
His reporting focuses on elections, national security, and institutional affairs, tracking the decisions and conflicts that shape public life.

stories.summary: Chandrababu Naidu joins NDA leaders in Delhi ahead of Parliament’s special sitting, as the Union Cabinet’s Bill keeps the present ratio of seats among States until 2051

opening: Chandrababu Naidu joins NDA leaders in Delhi ahead of Parliament’s special sitting, as the Union Cabinet’s Bill keeps the present ratio of seats among States until 2051.
A similar attempt by the government was rejected in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session in April.
body: The Union Cabinet met here on Friday and is learnt to have cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, which is likely to be brought before the special sitting of Parliament beginning next week.

The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth to discuss the bill, which the government is keen to get passed in the special sitting of Parliament starting Monday.
The bill was brought in Parliament by the government during a special sitting in April, but it could not pass muster in the Lok Sabha.
The government has now claimed that it has the numbers to get the legislation through.
A two-thirds majority in both houses of Parliament is a must for.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
stories.title: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday disposed of a Public Interest Litigation filed by financial journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking directions to authorities to put in place measures enabling legal heirs to trace and claim unclaimed financial assets, including bank deposits, shares and mutual fund investments.

Noting that the Union Government, the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India have taken various administrative and regulatory steps to address the issue, the bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice R Mahadevan observed that judicial directions in that regard are not necessary.
At the same time, the bench placed on record its appreciation for Dalal for taking up a genuine public cause, saying that the case was an example of a responsible use of public interest litigation.
The bench also appreciated Advocate Prashant Bhushan for espousing the petitioners' cause with "passion and perseverance."

"The present proceedings were instituted not for securing any personal benefit but with the objective of protecting the financial interests of countless depositors, investors and their lawful claimants.
The petitioner has consistently drawn attention to the difficulties faced by ordinary citizens in identifying and recovering the unclaimed financial assets.
The concerns raised were genuine and the pursuit of the appropriate institutional measures to address them reflects a responsible exercise of public interest litigation," the bench observed.
However, the Court noted that the principal concerns raised have been substantially addressed by measures undertaken by the respondents (SEBI, RBI and the Department of Economic Affairs).

"We take on record the statements and assurances made in the respondents affidavits and expect the concerned authorities to continue the efforts towards improving the accessibility, efficiency, and transparency of the mechanism for identifying and recovering unclaimed financial assets.
No useful purpose will be served by keeping the petition pending for further monitoring of the regulatory measures already undertaken.
Any specific grievances concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law," the bench added.
The bench had reserved judgment on November 17.

stories.headline: Supreme Court warns of penalties for Yamuna pollution, reviews waste management progress
stories.title: Supreme Court warns of penalties for Yamuna pollution, reviews waste management progress
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has warned states and UTs of penalties for failing to curb Yamuna pollution, urging a multi-pronged approach beyond sewage treatment plants.
Real-time monitoring, stricter accountability, and comprehensive waste management plans are mandated to address pollution incidents and improve water quality across jurisdictions.
The Yamuna flows through several states and the Union Territory (UT) of Delhi, with major drains emptying into it.
Water quality at state borders is monitored only quarterly.
Incidents such as fish deaths, white foam and algal blooms will now require investigation.
The Supreme Court has stepped in, warning that states and UTs failing to control Yamuna pollution, whether through inefficiency or a lack of political will, will face penalties.

In its November 4, 2026 order, the court called for a multi-pronged approach to cleaning the Yamuna, rather than focusing solely on building more sewage treatment plants (STP), decentralised treatment facilities and biogas plants.
Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan said the court was neither a city planner nor an expert body, and that civic authorities must prepare a comprehensive plan.

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was directed to submit water quality data, including biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), faecal coliform and total suspended solids (TSS), at points where the Yamuna and major drains enter and exit each state, UT and district.
Major interstate drains must also be monitored.
States, UTs and districts will be held accountable if water quality deteriorates as the river passes through their jurisdictions.
The CPCB must also investigate pollution incidents, including fish deaths, floating white foam, eutrophication and algal blooms, and recommend remedial measures.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Seeking Removal Of Videos Of Italian Politician Questioning Indian Elections At Bharat Summit
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Seeking Removal Of Videos Of Italian Politician Questioning Indian Elections At Bharat Summit
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today dismissed a plea seeking the removal of social media videos featuring an Italian politician allegedly questioning the country's democratic system during the Bharat Summit 2026 organized by the Telangana Government in Hyderabad on November 13-14.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Aparesh Singh dismissed the plea after briefly hearing Advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmad for the petitioner, who also sought regulation of speeches made by foreigners in events organised in India.
The matter was listed today after it was mentioned before the CJI last week.
During the mentioning, Ahmad described the remarks as a direct intervention in India's democratic affairs.
He said that the Italian delegate had not only raised the slogan but also translated it for other delegates attending the event.

"The participation of a foreign political representative in an Indian political campaign in this manner, including the raising of derogatory slogans and making prejudice political statements including the public endorsement of a particular political party and its leadership, raises a serious concern regarding the extent to which foreign political representatives may participate in or endorse the domestic political activities of an Indian political party violating the limits of International diplomacy, relations, ethics and corners of domestic political activities of India political parties while present within the territory of India, thereby raising questions concerning the permissible limits of international diplomacy and diplomatic relations."

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu hill lamp to be lit tomorrow: Supreme Court’s ‘iron hand’ action
stories.title: Tamil Nadu hill lamp to be lit tomorrow: Supreme Court’s ‘iron hand’ action
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday suspended the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple’s board of trustees and handed over its administration to two former Madras High Court judges over the “wilful disobedience” of its order to light the Karthigai deepam on the deepathon atop Madurai’s Thiruppurankundram Hill.
A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi directed the Central Reserve.
Police Force (CRPF) to take charge of security at the hill and ordered that the lamp be lit on Saturday, November 28.
It also directed two receivers, former Madras High Court judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthiban, to ensure that the lamp is lit on the deepathoon or stone pillar.

The court said the chain of events indicates that executive authorities acted on the dictates of political bosses and sought an affidavit from the Tamil Nadu chief secretary explaining the sequence of events, including the production of communications and emails.
“There is prima facie administrative chaos in the state of Tamil Nadu, at least in Madurai district,” it said.

The court also issued notices to the chief secretary, DGP, Madurai district collector, members of the temple’s board of trustees, temple executive officers, and others, asking them to explain why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them for allegedly violating its order.
The C Joseph Vijay-led Tamil Nadu Government was accused of defying the Supreme Court’s November 20 interim order.
The ceremonial Karthigai Deepam was lit only at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on November 24, rather than at the deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai.
The Tamil Nadu administration’s move triggered protests, police action at the foothills, and contempt petitions before the Supreme Court.

The court slammed the report by Nishant Krishna, District Collector, Madurai, in which he shifted the blame on the board of trustees, saying they did not authorise the team which was to light the lamp.

“We are surprised that the collector, who is also executive magistrate, can take such a stand… Not satisfied with his preliminary report,” the bench said, adding that the report “reminds of the saying ‘you play dead, and I pretend to cry’.”
